title: Kling 3.0 vs Sora 2 after shutdown: what to use now
summary: Sora 2 is retired. Compare its former features with Kling 3.0, export old Sora work, and test a current replacement without unsupported quality claims.
body_markdown:
## Quick answer


**For a new video project, choose Kling 3.0 over Sora 2 because Sora is retired.**


OpenAI closed Sora’s app and web experience April 26, 2026 and says its API ended September 24. This is now a migration question, not a live quality contest: export old Sora work, then test Kling on the same brief before committing a production workflow.


Checked September 26, 2026. This article compares current documented availability with historical features. We did not run a same-prompt output benchmark or independently verify vendor quality claims. See[OpenAI’s shutdown notice](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001152-what-to-know-about-the-sora-discontinuation) and[Kuaishou’s Kling 3.0 release](https://ir.kuaishou.com/news-releases/news-release-details/kling-ai-launches-30-model-ushering-era-where-everyone-can-be) . Magic Hour publishes this comparison and offers video creation tools.


## Kling 3.0 vs Sora 2: the decision has changed


Before the shutdown, a Kling-versus-Sora comparison could ask which model produced a better clip for the same shot. In September 2026, that framing misleads a reader starting a new project. OpenAI says the Sora consumer experience is gone and the separate API has ended. Kling’s 3.0 series remains a model family to evaluate. Availability outranks subjective model rankings when a team must ship new work.


If you already used Sora, the useful question is different: which parts of your prompt, characters, images, audio, output files and review criteria can you carry to a current tool? Kling is one candidate. For a broader shortlist, read our[Sora 2 alternatives guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/sora-2-alternatives) . This page stays narrowly focused on Kling 3.0 as a replacement for a Sora workflow.

The table separates **documented capabilities** from output quality. “Supports multi-shot” does not prove that a particular brief will keep a character, logo or camera path consistent. Kling Video 3.0 and Video 3.0 Omni are related modes, not interchangeable settings; confirm which is selected before testing.


## What happened to Sora 2?


OpenAI’s[official discontinuation guidance](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001152-what-to-know-about-the-sora-discontinuation) says the Sora web and app experiences were discontinued on April 26, 2026, and its API on September 24, 2026. Its former[Sora explore page](https://sora.chatgpt.com/explore) is a historical destination, not a new-project signup path. OpenAI directs previous users to its[Sora sunset export flow](https://sora.chatgpt.com/sunset) . OpenAI says it will delete Sora user data after any final export window, if one is offered; export promptly and verify your archive rather than assuming a date not stated in the notice.


Sora 2 remains relevant in search because people have old projects, prompts, invoices and tutorials. It also matters historically:[OpenAI’s launch account](https://openai.com/index/sora-2/) described synchronized speech and effects, more realistic physical interactions and improved multi-shot direction. Those are OpenAI’s release claims about its former model, not evidence that it is still purchasable or superior to every current model.


## What Kling 3.0 offers now


Kuaishou announced a Kling 3.0 family in February 2026: Video 3.0, Video 3.0 Omni, Image 3.0 and Image 3.0 Omni. Its[official announcement](https://ir.kuaishou.com/news-releases/news-release-details/kling-ai-launches-30-model-ushering-era-where-everyone-can-be) describes text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video and in-video editing in the series. It says the video models can produce up to 15-second clips with native audio. Video 3.0 includes multi-shot prompting; Omni adds stronger reference-based generation and a storyboard in which users can specify duration, shot size, perspective, narrative and camera movement. These are vendor-documented controls, not our measured success rates.


Kling’s current[app](https://app.klingai.com/global/) and Magic Hour’s[Kling 3.0 model page](https://magichour.ai/models/kling-3-0) are more useful starting points than a 2025 Sora tutorial. Confirm the mode, region, plan and current limits in the interface before budgeting. A page that still shows a model name is not proof that every tier or route exposes every control.


## Which Sora workflow can Kling replace?


**Prompt-to-video:** Preserve the Sora prompt’s subject, action, environment, camera movement, duration, aspect ratio, dialogue and sound cues in separate notes. Recreate the same brief in Kling Video 3.0. The two systems interpret prose differently, so start with one representative shot rather than porting a large prompt library at once.


**Reference-led scenes:** Export permitted source images and final outputs. Test them as references in a supported Kling mode. For recurring characters, try Omni’s reference controls, but compare identity, clothing and voice across several attempts. Do not assume an old Sora character or likeness object can be transferred directly; obtain rights and consent for the new input path.


**Multi-shot stories:** Split the original storyboard into shot descriptions. Record shot duration, framing, movement, character continuity and audio requirements. Kling documents multi-shot control, but a storyboard switch does not guarantee a usable edit. Review transitions and audio at the final delivery size.


**Developer integration:** Do not swap a Sora model ID for a Kling ID and expect compatibility. Inventory deprecated API calls, job polling, webhooks, file retrieval, error mapping and storage. Rebuild the request contract against the new provider’s current docs, then replay a small representative set. The direct Magic Hour[AI video generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-video-generator) is a creator workflow; API teams should validate an exact supported endpoint separately.


## A reproducible replacement test


Use the same four briefs on each currently available candidate: a character action, a product interaction, a moving-camera scene and a dialogue or ambient-audio scene. Keep reference files, duration target, aspect ratio and acceptance criteria fixed where the tools permit. Save every attempt, not only the best sample. A model is useful when its accepted outputs meet the delivery brief with tolerable retries, cost and turnaround.


For each result, score: requested action; subject and object continuity; camera path; motion artifacts; audio timing and intelligibility; text or logo fidelity; resolution; moderation or processing failures; and required manual cleanup. Define “accepted” before generating. Calculate cost per accepted deliverable as total credits or spend across all attempts divided by accepted clips. This is a **testing method** for your team, not a claim that we have measured Kling against retired Sora today.


Example brief: “A 6-second product reveal. One red ceramic mug rotates on a wood table; camera makes a slow clockwise arc. Keep the white printed word NORTH readable, use soft daylight, and end with the handle facing right. No hands or extra objects.” Test whether the mug count, label, handle and ending pose survive the complete clip. Change one prompt variable at a time when a failure appears. For native sound, add a separate sound cue only after the visual path works.


## Export first; then rebuild what matters


Open[OpenAI’s sunset page](https://sora.chatgpt.com/sunset) while signed in to the Sora account and request Export. OpenAI says an email arrives when the archive is ready. Download it, confirm that expected clips are present and keep a second copy in storage you control. Keep permitted source images, original briefs, reference audio, edit decisions and delivery files together. The archive format and available data may vary; do not promise that a future platform will import Sora projects or characters as editable objects.


Next, classify each old project: finished asset needing only storage, reusable shot needing a new render, or repeatable workflow needing new tooling. Do not regenerate finished assets without a reason. For the repeatable group, run the small test above and choose a platform based on actual accepted outputs. That process captures more value than arguing about historical peak-quality examples.


## Pricing, rights and limits to check before switching


Do not use an old Sora subscription chart to budget a new project. Sora is retired. Kling plan pricing, credit consumption, commercial rights and access may change by region, duration, resolution, audio and mode; verify the current checkout and terms. Record failed or rejected attempts as well as accepted exports. If you work with a client’s likeness or product marks, confirm permission for every input and review the new provider’s license and retention terms.


A free trial can answer whether a workflow fits, but it may have a different model menu, watermark, queue, duration or rights from a paid plan. For repeat campaigns, price a representative job: ten accepted 6-second clips in your required aspect ratio and resolution, including retries. That is more decision-useful than a price per generation that ignores rework.


## Who should use this comparison?


If you are choosing a video tool for a new campaign, evaluate Kling 3.0 and at least one other currently available model on your own shot list. If you only need to recover old Sora assets, start with OpenAI’s export notice rather than buying any new plan. If you need a larger cross-platform shortlist, use the[Sora alternatives guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/sora-2-alternatives) . If you are learning input methods, read[text-to-video versus image-to-video](https://magichour.ai/blog/text-to-video-vs-image-to-video-ai-tools) and the[best AI tools guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-tools-ranked) .


## Common questions


**Can I still generate with Sora 2?** OpenAI says its web/app experience closed April 26, 2026 and the API was discontinued September 24, 2026. Its current official notice is the authority if that status changes.


**Is Kling 3.0 objectively better than Sora 2?** This article cannot establish that. We have no current same-input Sora run and no controlled accepted-output dataset. Kling is the practical option for a new project because the Sora route is retired; quality still depends on the brief.


**Should I use Kling 3.0 or Kling 3.0 Omni?** Kuaishou describes Video 3.0 for multi-shot and native-audio generation, with Omni adding reference-led character and storyboard controls. Choose the available mode that matches your actual input and check the current model selector.


**Does Magic Hour only transform existing footage?** No. Magic Hour has[text-to-video](https://magichour.ai/products/text-to-video) ,[image-to-video](https://magichour.ai/products/image-to-video) , and[video-to-video](https://magichour.ai/products/video-to-video) routes. The right entry point depends on whether you start with a prompt, a still image or footage.


**What if I need a Sora-like image or cinematic shot?** Try the same brief in currently available tools, record the full set of attempts and compare against your deliverable. Our[Kling 3.0 review](https://magichour.ai/blog/kling-30-review) provides more Kling-specific context, while the alternatives guide covers the broader market.


### Test a current video model


Bring one Sora-era brief or reference image, generate a short sample, and check the complete result against your original acceptance criteria.
